analysis.session_summary: USD led the session with +0.236% strength and DXY +0.223%, leaving EUR/USD -17.3 pips, USD/JPY +74.8 pips, and USD/CHF +30.3 pips. The move lacked a scorable catalyst: Bessent's speech was unscored but USD/CHF +0.061% at 3.35σ, while GBP's Claimant Count miss (27.8K vs 8.3K) moved the basket only -0.029%. Oil headlines from the East-West pipeline closure and Hormuz kept two-way risk, but CAD still closed +0.174%. JPY and CHF were weakest, with JPY giving back 91% of an early +0.10% attempt.

themes.theme: Broad USD strength without hard catalyst
themes.evidence: USD strength +0.236%, DXY +0.223%; Bessent speech unscored but USD/CHF +0.061% at 3.35σ
Saudi pipeline cancellation moved USD/CAD -6.6 pips in 15 min (38% of leg); Brent up-leg +3.038%
Claimant Count 27.8K vs 8.3K forecast produced only a -0.029% GBP basket move
JPY -0.247% and CHF -0.134%; JPY gave back 91% of early +0.10% attempt

currency_drivers.USD: Broad strength held its range; Bessent speech gave a 0.044% unscored USD lift.
currency_drivers.EUR: No catalyst; selling to -0.05% was rejected, closing +0.086%.
currency_drivers.JPY: No catalyst; early +0.10% attempt gave back 91%, closing -0.247%.
currency_drivers.GBP: High-impact Claimant Count miss was muted, leaving GBP +0.056%.
currency_drivers.AUD: No catalyst; recovered from -0.141% to close at +0.035% best.
currency_drivers.CAD: Saudi pipeline cancellation headline supported CAD; closed +0.174%.
currency_drivers.CHF: No catalyst; early +0.05% attempt gave back 78%, closing -0.134%.
currency_drivers.NZD: No catalyst; weakest commodity FX at -0.207% in a held range.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: Three legs chopped within a 34.0-pip range: an uncatalyzed -30.0-pip Asia drop, a +20.9 recovery, and a Bessent-related -6.4 drift to close -17.3 pips.

polarity_reads.read: Unscored because no forecast; USD basket gained 0.044%, most visible in USD/CHF +0.061% (3.35σ), implying the market used it as a dollar-positive excuse rather than a clean surprise.
Muted: actual 27.8K vs 8.3K forecast should be GBP-negative but the basket moved only -0.029%, suggesting the market had already priced UK labor softening or ignored it amid oil/risk.

scenarios.name: USD strength extends after firm US data
scenarios.thesis: USD's +0.236% strength survives GBP CPI and is reinforced by retail sales at/above forecast.
triggers: US Core Retail Sales m/m prints at or above 0.6%
scenarios.invalidation: DXY closes back below 99.304 or Retail Sales misses.

pair_paths.rationale: Euro has no catalyst; repeats today's -17.3 pip decline.
JPY is weakest; USD/JPY already gained 74.8 pips today.

scenarios.name: USD profit-taking pullback
scenarios.thesis: After a +0.236% USD day with no hard catalyst, early Asia sees long-dollar positions trimmed.
scenarios.invalidation: DXY prints a new session high above 99.304.

pair_paths.rationale: Bounces within today's 34.0-pip range after closing -17.3.
CHF recovers some of today's +30.3 pip USD/CHF move.

scenarios.name: Hot UK CPI re-rates GBP
scenarios.thesis: GBP CPI y/y comes in above forecast 3.1% and forces hawkish BoE repricing, lifting GBP against EUR.
scenarios.invalidation: GBP CPI y/y prints at or below forecast 3.1%.

pair_paths.rationale: EUR/GBP falls through today's 15.0-pip range on GBP repricing.
GBP/USD recovers today's -24.1 pip drop if USD strength pauses.

risks.risk: Geopolitical escalation in Strait of Hormuz
risks.why_it_matters: Oil supply headlines can dominate CAD/NOK and risk FX, outweighing calendar data.
Can break EUR/GBP out of today's 15.0-pip range and reprice BoE.
USD +0.236% is not scorable; weak data could unwind DXY from 99.304.
risks.watch: 14:30 Retail Sales m/m forecast 0.8% prior -0.6%, Core 0.6%.

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: The next window has GBP CPI y/y (forecast 3.1% vs prev 2.9%) at 08:00 and US Retail Sales m/m (0.8% vs -0.6%) plus Core (0.6% vs -0.3%) at 14:30. A hot CPI or strong US sales extends USD, while misses would test the +0.236% USD move.
